clue.text: Having last word about copper's judgement

indicators.note: the closing word goes around the chemical symbol, so about signals one piece holding another

parts.note: amen is the word said at the end of a prayer
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: Someone credited with good judgement because they always get the final say over a policeman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a police officer, but it is the metal, giving its chemical symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Acumen is keen insight, the ability to make sharp decisions, a close synonym of good judgement.

clue.text: Benign atomic power supply taken under M1

indicators.note: in a down entry, a piece placed under another follows it, so the supply line comes after the motorway

parts.note: A as in A-bomb, the atomic bomb
the M1 motorway, read as the letters M and I
a cable carries electrical power

explanation.surface: A nuclear power line routed beneath Britain's main motorway is presented as harmless.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway; here its 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Amicable means friendly and well-disposed, and benign is a near synonym for kindly and gentle.

clue.text: Unemployed force supervised church for government-in-exile

parts.note: free in the sense of not occupied or engaged
ran, as in ran a team or project
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A jobless soldiery overseen by the church sounds like an odd sort of exiled administration.
explanation.walkthrough: Free France was de Gaulle's London-based wartime movement opposing the Vichy regime.
explanation.definitionFit: The Free French under de Gaulle operated from London as France's government outside occupied territory during the war.

clue.text: Sculptor with initial cast shows ruler in Asgard

indicators.note: cast here means thrown off, so the sculptor's first letter is discarded

parts.note: Auguste Rodin, French sculptor of The Thinker

explanation.surface: An artist's work, initially cast in bronze, depicts the king of the Norse gods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' suggests casting a statue, which suits a sculptor, but it means thrown away.
explanation.definitionFit: Odin is the chief god of Norse mythology, who presides over Asgard, home of the gods.

clue.text: Weary Willie clear in explosive tweet

indicators.note: the blank piece goes inside the rearranged letters
an explosive message is blown apart, so the letters of tweet are scattered

parts.note: the word itself, taken as written to be rearranged
blank as in a clear, empty page

explanation.surface: A tired-looking chap called Willie appears clean-cut in an angry social media post.
explanation.walkthrough: Weary Willie is an old name for a gloomy, listless person, not a real man.
explanation.definitionFit: A wet blanket is a killjoy who dampens enthusiasm, the same dispirited figure as a Weary Willie.

clue.text: Mark needs answer coming into Senior Common Room

indicators.note: the letter enters the abbreviation, sitting inside it

parts.note: SCR, the staff lounge at a British college

explanation.surface: Someone needs an answer to arrive at the dons' lounge before a mark is awarded.
explanation.definitionFit: A scar is a lasting blemish left on the skin by a wound, a kind of mark.

clue.text: Sick wife posh Eleanor nurses

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold close, so the name cradles the letter for wife

parts.note: U means upper-class, from the old U and non-U distinction
Nell is a pet form of Eleanor

explanation.surface: A smart woman called Eleanor looks after a poorly wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nurses' fits the sick wife in the surface, but it means holds inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Unwell and sick both describe someone in poor health or suffering an illness.

clue.text: Language without appeal applied to Krypton

indicators.note: the appeal piece is attached after the element symbol

parts.note: sans is French for without, used in English too
Kr is the chemical symbol for krypton
it as in sex appeal

explanation.surface: A tongue so lacking charm it might as well be from Superman's planet Krypton.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanskrit is the ancient classical tongue of India, a language of Hindu scripture.

clue.text: Infamous 26s mangled in big farm device

definitions.note: 26 is MOLE, so these are notorious spies; the plural matches the group's five members

indicators.note: mangled means crushed out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the clue words themselves, taken as written to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Notorious creatures crushed by a large piece of farm machinery.
explanation.walkthrough: 26 is MOLE: the moles in the surface are animals caught in a combine, but the answer is a spy ring.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cambridge Five were Soviet agents recruited at university who penetrated British intelligence, the most notorious spies of their era.

clue.text: Dance company now gives advice for beginners

parts.note: Co is the business abbreviation for company

indicators.note: only the starting letters of the following words are used

parts.note: the clue words themselves, whose first letters are taken

explanation.surface: A dance troupe now offers tips to novice dancers.
explanation.definitionFit: The conga is a Latin American dance performed in a long single-file line.

clue.text: 26 in manacles, almost broken

definitions.note: refers to 26-down, MOLE, here a spy

indicators.note: something broken has its parts in disorder, so the letters are rearranged
the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: the word itself, taken as written before being shortened

explanation.surface: A mole caught in chains has nearly broken free.
explanation.walkthrough: Donald Maclean was one of the Cambridge Five who spied for the Soviet Union.
explanation.definitionFit: Maclean was a British diplomat secretly passing secrets to Moscow, a classic intelligence mole.

clue.text: 26 needs to stop nonsense

definitions.note: refers to 26-down, MOLE, here a spy

indicators.note: a stopper plugs a gap, so this piece fills the middle of the other

parts.note: BS, short for a vulgar word for nonsense
urges, as in strong desires or wants

explanation.surface: A mole must put an end to all this rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: Guy Burgess was one of the Cambridge Five who defected to Moscow in 1951.
explanation.definitionFit: Burgess was a British intelligence insider working for the Soviets, a textbook example of a mole.

clue.text: No Scots bizzy initially making arrest

parts.note: na is the Scots word for no

indicators.note: only the first letter of the slang word for a policeman is taken

parts.note: bizzy is northern English slang for a police officer, here giving its first letter

explanation.surface: A Scottish police officer declines to make an arrest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scots' looks like describing the bizzy, but it tells you to say no the Scottish way.
explanation.definitionFit: To nab is informal for catching or apprehending, which is what a police arrest does.

clue.text: Charlie Brown wears uniform like certain figures

indicators.note: a wearer sits inside the clothing, so these letters go within the other piece

parts.note: regular in the sense of even or consistent
C in the NATO phonetic alphabet
tan is a light brown colour

explanation.surface: The Peanuts cartoon boy Charlie Brown dresses in uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charlie Brown' looks like one name, but it splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Rectangular describes shapes with four right angles, as squares and oblongs are, a kind of geometric figure.

clue.text: Stones on grave and Christian symbol for 26

definitions.note: refers to 26-down, MOLE, here a spy

parts.note: a cairn is a heap of stones, often marking a burial
the cross of the Crucifixion

explanation.surface: A burial mound of stones topped by a cross commemorates a mole.
explanation.walkthrough: John Cairncross is generally named as the fifth man of the Cambridge Five.
explanation.definitionFit: Cairncross passed British secrets, including Bletchley material, to the Soviet Union while employed by Whitehall, so he was a mole.

clue.text: Mouth that is opened by monarch reveals dry area

parts.note: gob is British slang for mouth

indicators.note: the monarch's letters split the Latin phrase open and sit in the middle

parts.note: id est, the Latin behind i.e.
ER, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A queen prising open someone's mouth exposes a parched patch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That is' must be the full Latin id est, not just IE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gobi is a vast arid region of Mongolia and China, a desert being land with little rainfall.

clue.text: Good of heathen to go for Spain's exultation

indicators.note: one letter leaves and another takes its place

parts.note: a pagan is a heathen, a non-believer
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: A godless person taking a Spanish turn leads to rejoicing.
explanation.definitionFit: A paean is a song of praise or triumph, an expression of joyful exultation.

clue.text: Pump for shipping line?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a canvas sports shoe
second meaning: the load line painted on a ship's hull

explanation.walkthrough: 'Shipping line' suggests a ferry company; the question mark flags the hull marking instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Plimsoll names both a rubber-soled gym shoe and the Plimsoll line showing how deep a vessel may be loaded.

clue.text: Is this essential for fluidity in writing?

definitions.meaning: sounds like a question about a smooth prose style
read literally, the liquid that pens need to write at all

explanation.walkthrough: Fluidity in writing usually means elegant style; here it is the literal fluid flowing from a pen.
explanation.definitionFit: Ink is the coloured liquid used by pens, without which nothing flows onto the paper.

clue.text: 26 not subtle with cannabis cigarette

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Anthony ..., the Cambridge Five mole
second meaning: ... as in direct and outspoken
third meaning: a cigar hollowed and filled with cannabis

explanation.surface: A mole who makes no secret of smoking a joint.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthony Blunt was the art historian exposed as a Soviet spy; the word also means frank, and is slang for a marijuana cigar.

clue.text: Entrails in pastry from pub Emile renovated

indicators.note: a renovated building is made over, so these letters are rebuilt in a new order

parts.note: the clue words themselves, taken as written to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Offal pie served by a refurbished bar run by someone called Emile.
explanation.walkthrough: Umble pie is the source of the phrase eat humble pie; umbles are a deer's innards.
explanation.definitionFit: Umble pie was a dish of deer offal baked in a crust, so it is literally innards inside a pie.

clue.text: Suffused nitrogen going into stew of red pig meat

indicators.note: the element symbol enters the jumbled letters
a stew mixes its ingredients, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the clue words themselves, taken as written to be rearranged
N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

explanation.surface: A casserole of pork soaked through with nitrogen gas.
explanation.definitionFit: Impregnated means saturated or permeated throughout, as suffused describes something spread through completely.

clue.text: Stuff on radio in respect of 26

definitions.note: refers to 26-down, MOLE, here a spy

indicators.note: broadcast speech is heard, not seen, so the word is rendered by its sound

parts.note: fill, as in stuff a cushion
by, as in a word meaning per or regarding

explanation.surface: Padding out a radio broadcast about a notorious spy.
explanation.walkthrough: Kim Philby was the most damaging of the Cambridge Five and fled to Moscow in 1963.
explanation.definitionFit: Philby rose high in MI6 while passing its secrets to the KGB, the archetype of a mole.

clue.text: Bloody awful performance: heads roll

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so the opening letters are taken

parts.note: the clue words themselves, whose first letters are taken

explanation.surface: After a dreadful show, someone in charge gets sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heads roll' reads as a set phrase for dismissals, but 'roll' is the definition. A bap is a soft bread roll.
explanation.definitionFit: A bap is a British soft bread bun, one kind of bread roll.

clue.text: Secretary with Spanish wine lying open

parts.note: PA, personal assistant
tent is an old name for a dark red Spanish wine

explanation.surface: A secretary with a bottle of Spanish wine is caught out lying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lying' seems to mean telling untruths, but it is part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Patent means exposed or unobstructed, as a duct is called patent when it remains unblocked.

clue.text: Cook slowly internalises pounds, having lost weight?

definitions.note: a comparative adjective, thinner than before

indicators.note: to internalise is to take inside, so this piece goes within the other

parts.note: to simmer is to cook gently just below the boil
L, from libra, the pound weight and sterling sign

explanation.surface: Slow cooking soaks up the pounds, yet the dieter comes out thinner.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that the answer is a comparative.
explanation.definitionFit: Slimmer is the comparative of slim, describing someone who is thinner after dieting.

clue.text: Spot with pigment, some Michelangelo made up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top, backwards
only some of the letters of the phrase are used, a run sitting across the words

parts.note: the run ELOM straddles the end of Michelangelo and the start of made

explanation.surface: Someone sees a coloured spot in a painting Michelangelo created.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes ELOM from the two words, and 'up' reverses it in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A mole is a small dark pigmented patch on the skin, so it is a pigmented spot.

clue.text: Female when given exam first to finish

parts.note: as, in the sense of while
a test

explanation.surface: A woman, when sitting an exam, is the first to hand in her paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Fastest means quickest of all, so the fastest runner is the first one over the line.

clue.text: See 9
Smear with 18?

definitions.meaning: 18 is INK, so a slur written down rather than spoken

explanation.walkthrough: 18-across is INK: a smear made with ink sounds like a blot, but it is a written slander.
explanation.definitionFit: Libel is defamation in written or printed form, an attack on reputation set down in writing.

clue.text: Charles done with throne at last? Omen about that!

indicators.note: the omen surrounds the other letters

parts.note: a sign, a portent
over, as in finished

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word is taken

parts.note: the word itself, whose final letter is taken

explanation.surface: Charles has finished with the throne at last; a portent surrounds the moment.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles reads as a person, but the definition is the title he holds.
explanation.definitionFit: King Charles III is the reigning monarch, and a sovereign is a supreme ruler.
